excerpt: In the set S = {a, b, c} case, Schaffer treats c's membership as relevant to S having exactly three members, but the source argues that counterfactual necessity cannot consistently explain both the three-member and finite-member steps.
overview: The passage undercuts an existing non-transitivity argument before presenting the paper's own. It shows that Schaffer's case depends on shifting from counterfactual necessity as a support for grounding to counterfactual necessity as a bar against grounding, while determinable-determinate and disjunctive grounding cases resist that shift.
title: Schaffer Test Inconsistency
